# ECN-2026-011 Change notice - Hot Forge induction billet heater #3

Revision: Rev B  
Plant: P1, line P1-L1  
Equipment: EQ-P1-L1-IH03

Reason for change
- Background: Recent inspection and trending of heater performance identified repeated low coil cooling water flow events that correlate with control trips and degraded billet heating uniformity on Hot Forge induction billet heater #3 (EQ-P1-L1-IH03). The investigation determined that the effective minimum flow required to prevent coil overheating and to maintain stable power coupling is higher than the conservative operational threshold currently documented in maintenance checklists.
- Safety and quality rationale: Maintaining sufficient coil cooling water flow prevents premature insulation degradation, reduces electrical arcing risk, and supports stable process control that affects billet microstructure consistency. The change aligns minimum flow requirements with observed operational limits to reduce unplanned downtime and nonconforming forged parts.
- Regulatory and procedural alignment: This ECN implements the engineering change mandated by the equipment reliability review and ensures related maintenance and operational procedures are updated in accordance with MM-P1-L1-IH03-S3 and QS-PROC-01. A service bulletin is issued for immediate field awareness (see SB-1009).

Affected items
- Equipment: Induction billet heater identified as EQ-P1-L1-IH03 (Hot Forge induction billet heater #3).
- Documentation: Maintenance procedures and operator checklists in MM-P1-L1-IH03-S3; process control and nonconformance handling in QS-PROC-01; plant service bulletin SB-1009.
- Controls and alarms: Pump interlock and flow indication logic related to coil cooling water for EQ-P1-L1-IH03. Control system setpoints and alarm thresholds shall be reviewed and adjusted to reflect the new minimum flow requirement.
- Records and logs: Flow verification records, maintenance intervention reports, and corrective action records will be updated and maintained as described in the Implementation section.

Implementation
- Change description: Establish the coil cooling water flow minimum for EQ-P1-L1-IH03 as 72 L/min and update all relevant control setpoints, operator instructions, and maintenance documentation to reference this value exactly as written.
- Procedure updates: Revise MM-P1-L1-IH03-S3 to include:
  - A mandatory flow verification step at shift handover and after pump maintenance that records measured flow versus the specified minimum of 72 L/min.
  - A procedural pause and escalation path if measured flow is below 72 L/min, including immediate notification of maintenance and process engineering and placement of the heater into a safe state per QS-PROC-01.
- Control system changes: Update the programmable logic controller and human-machine interface alarm thresholds so that low-flow alarm annunciates when measured flow falls below 72 L/min. Alarm response text must direct operators to follow the updated steps in MM-P1-L1-IH03-S3.
- Physical work: Inspect the cooling circuit hardware, clean strainers, and verify pump performance where indicated by troubleshooting. If corrective hardware work is required, document findings and actions in maintenance records and reference SB-1009 for guidance on interim operating limits and field advisories.
- Training and communication: Conduct targeted training sessions for operators and maintenance technicians covering the new minimum flow requirement of 72 L/min, revised control behavior, and the procedural steps from MM-P1-L1-IH03-S3. Maintain attendance records and competency confirmation as required by QS-PROC-01.
- Examples of application: 
  - Example scenario A: During a routine shift check, the operator measures coil cooling water flow below the required minimum. The operator places EQ-P1-L1-IH03 in standby per MM-P1-L1-IH03-S3, records the measured value, notifies maintenance and process engineering, and follows SB-1009 for interim safety measures until flow is restored to at least 72 L/min.
  - Example scenario B: Post-pump maintenance, the technician performs a verification run and documents a measured flow meeting or exceeding the minimum. The technician completes the post-maintenance checklist and signs off in the maintenance log as prescribed by MM-P1-L1-IH03-S3.
- Verification and acceptance: After changes are implemented, perform a validation run to demonstrate stable heater operation with recorded coil cooling water flow at or above 72 L/min and normal power coupling behavior. Document results in the equipment validation record and attach to the ECN closure package.

Records to keep
- Updated MM-P1-L1-IH03-S3 with revision history noting this ECN.
- Control system change request and implementation log showing updated alarm thresholds tied to the 72 L/min minimum.
- Training attendance roster and competency confirmations as required by QS-PROC-01.
- Post-change validation report and trend data demonstrating heater stability at or above 72 L/min.
- Maintenance logs and any corrective action reports generated as a result of low-flow events, with reference to SB-1009 when interim measures were applied.

Approvals
- Engineering review: Approval required to implement control logic and documentation changes.
- Maintenance authorization: Approval required for any hardware interventions and for release of the equipment to operations following repairs.
- Operations acceptance: Sign-off required confirming operator training completion and adherence to revised procedures.
- Quality oversight: Quality assurance verification that changes comply with QS-PROC-01 and that records meet system retention requirements.

References
- MM-P1-L1-IH03-S3
- QS-PROC-01
- SB-1009

Document control
- ECN identifier: ECN-2026-011 Rev B
- Affected equipment: EQ-P1-L1-IH03
- Plant location: P1, line P1-L1

End of change notice.
